analysis.one_liner: Samvardhana Motherson International is a global auto-component maker that builds wiring harnesses, mirrors, plastics, modules and other parts for carmakers worldwide, grown via both internal expansion and a long string of acquisitions.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results (quarter ended Sep 2026) were announced on 5 Nov 2026 - inside the last two weeks. Revenue rose 27% YoY to a record ₹38,280 crore and reported net profit rose 44% YoY to ₹1,217.6 crore (normalised PAT ₹1,175 crore), with a record $106 billion order book. Despite this, the stock fell 8-9% on results day because EBITDA margin slipped about 20 basis points to roughly 8.8-9% (management blamed integration of recently acquired businesses) and EPS of ₹0.98 missed the ₹1.02 consensus. Most brokerages still raised targets (JPMorgan ₹205, Jefferies ₹200, Goldman Sachs ₹176, Nomura ₹190), but CLSA was a sharp outlier, cutting its target from ₹190 to ₹127. The stock has since recovered part of the fall, closing at ₹159.4 on 8 Nov against a ₹170.68 peak hit on 31 Aug 2026.
analysis.plain_terms: This is India's largest auto-parts exporter, selling wiring, mirrors and plastic parts to carmakers globally - growth has come from both selling more and buying other companies. The latest quarter shows strong revenue and profit growth, but the profit margin dipped slightly because newly bought businesses aren't yet running as efficiently as the core business. The tension: management says the underlying margin (excluding new acquisitions) actually improved, but hasn't put a number on that claim, so it can't be verified here. With the stock priced at roughly 35 times earnings, the market has little tolerance for that kind of wobble, which is why a result with 27% revenue growth and 44% profit growth still triggered a near 9% share price drop.
analysis.quarters: Revenue has climbed every quarter: Q3 FY26 ₹30,212 crore (margin ~8%, PAT ₹606 crore) to Q4 FY26 ₹34,309 crore (margin ~11%, PAT ₹1,562 crore) to Q1 FY27 ₹35,244 crore (margin ~9%, PAT ₹1,076 crore) to Q2 FY27 ₹38,280 crore (margin ~8.8-9%, PAT ₹1,218 crore, normalised ₹1,175 crore). The wiring-harness segment alone went from ₹8,550 crore to ₹14,382 crore YoY - a jump too large to be organic volume alone, so recent acquisitions are doing real work in that growth number. Management said Q2 margin improved YoY and sequentially once acquisition-integration effects are stripped out, but did not disclose that adjusted figure - treat that specific claim as Not verified. Sources vary on the exact EBITDA margin (8.4%, 8.8%, 9% have all been quoted); the differences likely reflect EBITDA vs. reported operating-profit definitions rather than a real discrepancy.
analysis.performance_read: The 1-year return of +56% looks spectacular against the Nifty's -2.3% and peer Bosch's +37%, but the 3-month return has flipped to -5% while the Nifty is up 1.6% and Bosch is up nearly 17% - so some of that 1-year gain has already reversed, largely around this results reaction. Over 3 years the stock (+170%) has roughly matched Bosch (+169%), both well ahead of the Nifty (+29%), but over 5 years the stock (+151%) has trailed Bosch (+199%) - the longer window favours the peer. The current price is only 6.6% below the all-time high hit in August 2026 - this is a mild pullback, not a crash. The stock has gone through nine 1.5-for-1 stock splits since 2002 (most recently July 2025); these are routine liquidity-improving splits, not demergers or spin-offs, so no return addback is needed - the return figures above are already split-adjusted.
analysis.valuation_read: The stock trades around 34.7x trailing earnings and 3.7x book value (per the most current cross-checked source); an older snapshot showed 38.9x/3.9x, which is set aside as dated rather than averaged in. Against an ROE of just 11.2% (11.7% on a 3-year average) and ROCE of 13.4%, a mid-30s P/E is rich on raw profitability - the market is paying up for the record $106 billion order book and acquisition-fuelled growth story, not for current return ratios. Whether that premium is justified depends on whether the margin dip seen this quarter is a one-off integration cost or a sign that recently acquired businesses structurally earn less. Dividend yield is a thin 0.38% - this is priced and run as a growth/reinvestment story, not an income stock.
analysis.growth_read: Revenue grew 27% YoY, but a large part of that - visible in the wiring-harness segment's revenue nearly doubling YoY - comes from recently acquired businesses consolidating into the numbers, not purely from selling more of the existing book of business. Margin moved down slightly alongside this growth rather than up, so this reads as volume/inorganic-led growth with a margin drag attached, not margin-led growth. The true organic, ex-acquisition margin trend that management referenced on the call was not disclosed with a number, so it stays Not verified here.
analysis.health_read: Leverage looks conservative - debt-to-equity around 0.4x on a cross-checked source (one data pull showed an equity base too small relative to market cap to be reliable, so that specific absolute borrowings/net-worth figure is Not verified and was set aside rather than used). Profit growth (reported PAT +44% YoY) tracked with EBITDA growth (₹3,353-3,357 crore) rather than diverging sharply, suggesting this quarter's profit is operating-cash-backed rather than driven by one-off items, though full cash-flow-to-profit conversion for the quarter could not be independently verified from the sources checked. Given the low leverage, the more relevant risk here is business risk - margin dilution from digesting several recent acquisitions in a cyclical, auto-OEM-dependent end market - rather than financial/balance-sheet risk.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters (the Sehgal family / Samvardhana Motherson group) held a steady 48.6% as of the September 2026 quarter, unchanged from the prior quarter. Promoter pledge is small and stable at 2.34% - not a current red flag. Institutional ownership is broad rather than concentrated: FIIs around 13%, and mutual funds (Quant, ICICI Prudential Manufacturing, Motilal Oswal Manufacturing, LIC-linked schemes among others) each holding low single-digit stakes. No well-known individual 'star' investor appears on the public shareholding register - ownership here is institutional, not retail-guru-driven.
strengths: Record Q2 FY27 revenue of ₹38,280 crore, up 27% YoY
Record booked business / order book of $106 billion, giving multi-year revenue visibility
Conservative balance sheet with debt-to-equity around 0.4x
Promoter holding stable at 48.6% with a low, unchanged pledge of 2.34%
watchpoints: EBITDA/operating margin slipped about 20 bps YoY to roughly 8.8-9% on acquisition-integration costs, with no disclosed timeline to normalise
Reported EPS of ₹0.98 missed the ₹1.02 consensus, which alone triggered an 8-9% one-day share price fall despite broker target hikes
Valuation is rich at ~35x trailing earnings against an ROE near 11%, leaving little room for further execution slips
CLSA cut its target sharply from ₹190 to ₹127 - a notable dissent from the broadly bullish broker consensus, worth tracking for why
analysis.one_thing: Whether EBITDA margin recovers back toward the 9-11% band over the next 1-2 quarters as newly acquired businesses are integrated - that resolves whether this quarter's dip was temporary integration noise or a more lasting margin reset.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 revenue (₹38,280 crore) and the 42-44% YoY profit growth were consistent across autocarpro, freepressjournal, zeebiz and tradingview. EBITDA/operating margin was cited inconsistently (8.4%, 8.8%, 9%) across sources - likely different definitions (EBITDA vs. operating profit) rather than genuine conflict; used screener.in's 9% operating margin as the primary reference. One source's absolute borrowings/net-worth figures looked internally inconsistent given the company's market cap, so those specific numbers were set aside as Not verified in favour of a cross-checked D/E ratio of ~0.4x. Management's claim of improved underlying (ex-acquisition) margin was not accompanied by a disclosed figure and is flagged as Not verified. Cash-flow-to-profit conversion for the quarter specifically could not be independently confirmed from the sources reviewed.
